Commentary.Commentary: After Smith's dismissal, the hosts lost 7/67. That sums up Australia's dependency on their best batsman. Credit must go to the Englishmen for triggering a collapse and not letting the intensity drop throughout. However, on a sluggish surface, 327 can prove to be competitive. Let's see how the away side respond with the bat. Join us back shortly.

Earlier, Australia got off to a good start courtesy their openers, especially David Warner who struck a magnificent ton. The skipper Steven Smith came in and was at his usual best. It seemed that the tourists will once again get pummeled into submission by the heroics of the Australian skipper but that wasn't to be. Shaun Marsh too scored a fine fifty but couldn't carry on while Tim Paine didn't last long either.

England have only taken 20 minutes after Lunch, 24 balls to be precise to bowl the hosts out. An inspirational bowling performance from them means that Australia have packed up for their lowest first innings total at the MCG since 2011. The stars for the visitors were their frontline bowlers, Broad and Anderson. They shared 7 wickets between them and broke the backbone of the home side.

OUT! Umpire's call and England have done extremely well to restrict Australia under 350. Once again the shiny side of the ball is on the inside. Gets prodigious reverse swing on that as Lyon loses his balance in an attempt to flick it away. Misses it completely to get hit on the pads. The hosts roar in appeal and the umpire obliges. Lyon opts for the DRS. There is no bat involved. It's in line and would have clipped the leg stump. That is it! AUSTRALIA ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 327!
Lyon seems to be a goner but he has opted for the review...
Reverses in prodigiously but goes down the leg side, Lyon misses his glance.
Length ball around off, kept out watchfully.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Ooh... the substantial inward movement almost caught Lyon napping. The shiny side is on the inside and the ball reverses in. Nathan plants his front foot across and keeps it out tentatively out to mid-wicket.
Lyon gets nicely behind the line of the length delivery and defends it towards covers.
Fractionally overpitched, driven hard but finds the man at covers.

Another unconvincing stroke. Fullish ball, angling away, Hazlewood goes for a booming drive but skews it off the outer half towards backward point. The fielder dives full length to his right to make a good stop.
Good length ball on leg stump, the southpaw tries to play it across but is struck on the thigh pad.
Another play and a miss! On a drivable length outside off, Josh falls for the bait and gets beaten all ends up.
Fractionally overpitched around off, eased off the front foot to covers.
Fuller in length outside off, Josh is tentative again as he pushes it off the outer half of his bat to cover-point.
Hazlewood is off the mark and the packed crowd cheers for him. Tucks the length ball to mid-wicket for a brisk single and will retain strike.
Pitched right up there on middle, Josh with minimal foot movement plays it down the track.
Tentative from Josh. Leans ahead to counter the slower ball but the ball whizzes past his outside edge.
Back of a length ball on off, Hazlewood camps back and pushes it to mid off.
Angling away on a length from Josh. He keeps his bat inside the line and lets it go.
Well-directed bouncer on off, Hazlewood ducks under it in a jiffy.
James Anderson to bowl from the other end.
Leg cutter from Broad. Lyon tries to counter it but gets foxed.
Full length ball, patted to mid off.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Edged but safe! Angling in sharply from outside off, Lyon plays for the incoming angle and gets a thick outside edge that flies towards the fielder at gully but falls well short of the fielder.
Nathan Lyon is the last man in. He gets a rousing applause from the MCG crowd.

OUT! Yes, it is indeed a clean take from Alastair Cook. 4-fer for Stuart Broad and this is his 397th Test wicket, three short of a commendable landmark. He hurls this one on a drivable length outside off, Cummins goes for a booming drive but gets a fat outside edge. The English ex-skipper at first slip crouches and seems to have taken it just above the ground. However, the umpires decide to have a check regarding the clarity of the catch. The replays roll in and the replays confirm that it has been grabbed nicely. Another one bites the dust.
Cummins is walking back but he has been told to stop by the umpires. They are checking whether the catch by Cook at first slip is clean or not. Seems gone to the naked eye. The soft signal is out.
Pitched up delivery on off, pushed off the front foot to mid off.

We are back for the second session. Temperatures in the mid 30s, won't be an easy task for the bowlers. Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood to continue their innings. Will they throw their bat around and reach the 350-run mark? Or will England run through them in a flash? Stuart Broad to continue his spell. Here we go...
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

Stuart Broad was at his belligerent best and he was ably supported by James Anderson. They kept on hitting consistent lines and lengths and reaped the dividends to bring their side back into the game. With the track getting more two-paced as was amplified by the fact that there were three chop on dismissals in the morning, run-scoring won't be an easy affair. Australia will be expecting their tail to add as much as possible while the tourists will strive to clean it up in a jiffy. Join us for the afternoon session which promises to be a cracker!

Steven Smith and Shaun Marsh started the day off well but failed to continue the good work. The visitors needed to get rid of the Australian skipper early and that is what they did, courtesy Tom Curran who bagged his maiden Test wicket. The Marsh brothers also departed in quick succession handing the Englishmen an opening.

England have dominated the morning session! Yes, you heard it right. Picking up 5 wickets and not giving away too much is a commendable effort. They came out with intent this morning and fired on all cylinders. Credit must go to Joe Root who was spot on with his bowling changes and kept on attacking the batsmen.
Full ball outside off, driven wide of cover-point for a run. THAT SHALL BE LUNCH ON DAY 2!
Appreciable movement again. On a length outside off, seaming in. Cummins does well to get his bat down in time and keeps it out.
Full ball outside off, left alone.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On a length, played with an angled bat to point.
Back of a length outside off, played with soft hands to covers.
Josh Hazlewood walks out to the middle.
Bird looks dead to the naked eye but still he opts for the review against an LBW decision.

OUT! Plumb! Broad is breathing fire, picks up his third wicket. Good length ball around off, angling in appreciably and stays a bit low. Bird is caught in the crease as he tries to keep it out but misses to get pinged on the pads. The Englishmen appeal in unison and up goes the umpire's finger. Bird has a chat with his partner and challenges the decision. There is no inside edge as shown by the Snicko. The Hawk Eye rolls in. The impact is umpire's call and it is going on to crash the stumps.
Beaten for pace! Lovely bowling from Broad. Coming in substantially, Bird looks to block it but gets foxed.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Beautifully bowled! On a length outside off, coming in initially with the angle and moving away after hitting the deck. Cummins feels for it and is beaten all ends up.
Overpitched outside off, driven wide of cover for a brace.
Back of a length outside off, left alone.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Completely beats Bairstow for pace and an opportunity goes down! Full delivery outside off, a lot of nibble in the air. Bird goes for a drive with minimal foot movement and gets a thick outside edge. Jonny dives to his right but the ball goes past him in a flash and also beats Cook at first slip. A boundary results.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Jackson Bird comes out to bat.

OUT! England are back in the contest exclaims an excited Bill Lawry on air! Chopped on. This is the third time this has happened this morning. 520th Test wicket for Jimmy. With that, he goes past the legendary Courtney Walsh and becomes the second leading wicket-taker in terms of a pace bowler. This is the beauty of bowling closer to the stumps, you are always in with a chance when the batsman makes a mistake. Shortish delivery around off, Paine stands tall and goes for a full-fledged pull but only manages to get an inside edge which goes onto crash into the stumps. He had mistimed a pull earlier as well and falls trying to attempt it once again. The pair of Anderson and Broad is bringing in the rewards for the Englishmen.
On a length outside off, Paine lets it go.
Tight stuff! Full and attacking the stumps, blocked back down the track by Cummins.
Back of a length outside off, dabbed on the bounce towards gully.
Lovely bowling! Broad arrows it in from around off, Cummins looks to defend but the ball straightens to beat him all ends up. Stuart his bowling much better today, hitting the right lengths.
Pitches it up around off, almost a yorker, Pat lunges forward and digs it out towards cover.
On a length and holding its line a touch, Cummins plays inside the line and gets beaten.
Keeps it on a fuller length, probing line, Cummins makes a watchful leave.
A mistimed shot! Short ball outside off, Paine goes for the pull but doesn't get it off the meat. The ball rolls towards mid-wicket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Shaping in appreciably from a good length, Paine covers the line to block it nicely.
Back of a length outside off, played with an angled bat to point.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
FOUR! Well played! Loosener from Anderson. Short and it sits up nicely for Paine. He stands tall and pulls it with command through mid-wicket to find the fence.
Anderson is back on. Good move from Joe Root to bring his strike bowler on.
Pat Cummins strides out to bat.

OUT! No inside edge, what a judicious use of the review from England! Broad is over the moon and so are his teammates. He steams in from over the wicket and bowls a length ball on middle and leg. Gets it to seam in after pitching. Marsh puts in a nice stride forward to counter it but misses the line of the ball to get pinged on the front pad. Broad roars in an appeal along with his teammates but umpire S Ravi remains unmoved. He is on the run and tells Joe Root to challenge the decision and the skipper accepts. Time for the replays. The Snicko doesn't spot any nick. Now, the Hawk Eye rolls in. The ball has pitched in line, impact is in line and it is hitting the stumps. 'OUT' flashes the giant screen and the English camp is elated! A good knock from Marsh comes to an end. Yesterday, Stuart had caught Shaun napping on the first ball of his innings. It was reviewed but the hitting was umpire's call. This time the on-field call had to be reversed. One of England's strike bowlers is in the zone. Another vital breakthrough for the visitors. Game on!
Broad's followthrough shows that he is extremely confident that he has trapped Marsh in front of the stumps. He eggs his skipper to take the review and he agrees. Is there an inside edge?
On a length outside off, slanting away, played with an open bat face towards cover-point.
A bit uppish but safe! Fullish delivery, Marsh clips it nicely and it falls well short of the fielder at mid on.
Similar delivery, patted to mid on this time.
Full delivery on leg stump, blocked towards mid-wicket.
Length ball angling down leg, Marsh falls over a bit in a bid to flick it and wears it on his pads. Broad is excited for a while but realizes that it is going down leg.
Stuart Broad comes back for a bowl.
Length ball outside off, Paine pushes at it but mistimes it to the cover region. Perhaps the first false shot from him.
Fullish delivery, angling in, Paine is assured in his leave.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

FOUR! Shot of the day! Paine is flowing freely. Tossed up outside off, Paine drives it beautifully in the gap between mid off and extra cover to pick up another boundary. Textbook stuff from the wicket-keeper batsman.
Fullish delivery, clipped to mid on for a run.
Nicely done. Strides forward confidently to the tossed up ball and drives it wide of cover-point for a run.

Ian Chappell on air praises Tim Paine. It is not easy to adjust after losing a close member of the family. He lost his father-in-law on the Christmas Eve but still came back to play. He has come out with positive intent and is looking very confident. Sometimes tough times make you more determined to perform well.
FOUR! Shot! Fullish ball on middle, Marsh clears his front leg and strokes it towards mid on. Timing is spot on and away she whistles to the fence.
Slower in pace, kept out watchfully.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Floated outside off, eased down the track.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Amazing shot! Flighted ball outside off, Paine reaches to the pitch of the ball and drives it elegantly through covers. The substitute, Crane at sweeper cover goes to his right, slides but fails to keep the ball in play.
The intention was good but the execution was not. Goes for a slower yorker but ends up slipping it down the leg side. Marsh fails to pick it and is beaten on the flick. Good over from Curran.
Walks a couple of steps down the track and eases it to mid off for a single.
Slower ball which has been read well by Paine as he blocks it confidently.
Root has been proactive with his captaincy today. His bowling changes have brought productive results and his intensity has been also up. This is the way to lead by example.
Back of a length outside off, left alone.
Once again the two-paced nature of the track is evident! Shortish delivery outside off and room on offer, Paine goes for a cut but gets a bottom edge down on the track.
Length delivery just outside off, Paine lets it go.
Tom Curran returns for a burst.
Fullish on middle, defended solidly off the front foot.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Uses his feet to this one and drives it hard to Ali who makes a good stop.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.

Brilliant fielding! This is the kind of commitment you need from your players. Short and spinning away, Marsh nails the cut but the fielder at backward point dives to his left to save certain runs. Keeps it down to a single.
Slower in pace, patted towards short cover.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

FOUR! Poor fielding and the visitors pay the price for it. On a hot day with the temperatures soaring around 35 degrees, you need to support your bowlers. Overpitched around off, Paine leans into it and drives it towards wide mid off. The fielder moves to his left, puts in a lazy dive and makes a mess of it. Ends up conceding a boundary.
Fullish delivery, Paine defends it with a straight bat.
Fullish delivery on middle and leg, clipped nicely to fine leg for a run.
In the zone outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Brilliantly executed! Short of a length ball outside off, Marsh waits for it and steers it past the gully region to find the fence. Not an easy shot to play on a track which has become a bit two-paced.
Floated outside off, Paine creams it to sweeper cover. Finds the gap and hares back for the second.
Tossed up ball, defended solidly off the front foot.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.

9th Test fifty for Shaun Marsh! He is having a great Ashes, well played lad! Stays leg side of the ball and strokes it to covers for a swift single. Raises his bat towards the MCG crowd and sinks in all the applause. He needs to take more responsibility now after the fall of two quick wickets.
Tossed up outside off, eased to covers off the front foot.
Fuller in length, wristed towards wide mid on.

Time for Drinks. Good first hour for England. They have scalped two wickets, one being the big one of Steven Smith who was looking set. However, they will be aware of the fact that the Australian lower middle order has come to the rescue whenever the hosts have been in trouble. Shaun Marsh is out and is one short of a half century. Can he continue to bat on or will the visitors continue to chip away at the wickets?
Stays back and pushes it past Woakes as the ball rolls towards mid on.
Leans ahead and pushes it to mid off.
Probing line from Woakes, in the channel outside off, left alone.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Michael Clarke on air has got something to say regarding the pitch. He says, usually the pitch here tends to become slower as the game progresses. So, the best time to bat here is when the ball is new and it's kicking off the surface. When the ball becomes softer, the batsmen find it difficult to middle it.

Inside edge again! Fuller and around off, Paine looks to drive but the ball squirts off the inner half behind square on the leg side. Good running between the wickets allows them to come back for the second.
Shortish and outside off, Paine makes an easy leave.

FOUR! Good placement! Ali sees Marsh stepping out, so he shortens his length. What does Marsh do? He still walks out and with pure placement he guides it through point to end the over with a boundary. Moves to 49 with that.
Drifting in from around off, Marsh steps out and pushes it towards cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Marsh steps out of the crease but ends up yorking himself. Still manages to jam it out towards mid on.
Slower through the air, SM leans forward and pushes it towards cover.
Floats it up around middle and off, Marsh defends it off the front foot.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Paine shoulders his arms to that one. Another successful over for England.
Tim Paine walks out to the middle next.

OUT! Another one chops it back on! Is this the sign of the pitch being two-paced? Anyway, the bowling change has worked wonders for Root again. He removed Curran and brought Woakes and sees the back of the centurion from the last game. Superb from England! Chris Woakes from over the wicket, hurls it a bit wider outside off and this time the ball doesn't bounce as much as expected. Mitchell Marsh, just like his skipper, tries to go at it with hard hands. An inside edge has been induced as the ball bounces and then hits the top of off stump. Mitchell would be feeling unlucky here, as the ball could have bounced over the stumps but it hasn't. He has to walk back and Australia are in a bit of a tricky situation now.
Slightly shorter again, Mitchell Marsh blocks it off the back foot.
Good length delivery, wide outside off, left alone easily.
Shortish and angling in, Marsh turns it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Begins his spell with a shortish delivery outside off, Marsh stands tall and dabs it with an angled bat towards the gully fielder.

Chris Woakes is brought into the attack for the first time today. Interesting, Curran is taken off. He got the prized wicket of Smith. Is it because he gave away 8 in his last over the reason behind this? Either way, here comes Chris. A wide slip and a gully in place...
Goes back and clips it past the man at silly mid on.
Sliding in from around off, blocked solidly off the front foot and into the ground.
Short and around off, Marsh punches it towards backward point.
Goes flatter now, Marsh hangs back in defense.
Good shot from Mitchell! He has come out with good positive intent! Sees the flight, takes a stride ahead and drills it towards sweeper cover for a couple of runs.
Tosses it up outside off, MM lunges forward and kills it down.
Fuller and on off this time, defended off the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Curran is not getting it right to the left-hander! Sprays it on the pads yet again, Shaun Marsh gets inside the line and clips it neatly down to fine leg to pick up a boundary.
Another delivery on the pads, whipped down to long leg where Woakes does the mop up job. Two picked up again.
Fuller on the stumps, defended off the front foot.
Curran once again serves on the pads, luckily it's clipped straight towards mid-wicket.
Fuller and on the pads, clipped towards backward square leg for a double.
Drops it short on middle, defended off the back foot.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Loopy delivery outside off, Mitchell Marsh leans forward and with an open face bat he drives it wide of the cover fielder to collect a couple.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Quicker through the air and around off, defended again.
Flatter and around off, defended off the front foot and into the ground.
Moeen Ali is brought into the attack now.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. Successful over for Curran!
Punches it towards backward point where the fielder makes a good stop. A run taken.

FOUR! What a shot! That's some way to show the opposition that you are in form! Short and outside off, Marsh packs a punch. Gets it squarer and the man at backward point had no chance to stop that one.
Good length delivery, nipping back in a bit, defended by coming forward.
Mitchell Marsh is the next man in. He was absolutely on song in the last game. He's coming off a huge ton in Perth and it would be interesting to see how he goes.

OUT! Drags it on! Tom Curran gets the big fish, folks! And his landing is fine this time. Maiden Test wicket for him and he is up and running! What a moment for him. England have got the breakthrough and the bowling change has done the trick. He bowls it short and a bit wide outside off, Smith tries to force it through the off side but the ball bounces a bit more which leads to an inside edge. It then goes on to disturb the stumps. Steven Smith is finally dismissed for the first time in the Boxing Day Test since 2015, that's quite a remarkable feat. Now then, can England create further inroads?

Starts off with a back of a length delivery on middle, Marsh turns it towards Moeen Ali at mid-wicket and scampers through for a quick single. A handshake from the two batsmen as it brings up the 100-run stand between the two.
First change of the day then. Debutant Tom Curran is brought into the attack.
Angles it in on a good length, Smith defends it down gently.
Very full on off, Smith takes a stride forward and blocks it out.
Shortish in length and outside off, pushed off the back foot towards backward point.
Fuller in the channel outside off, left alone easily.

This is unnecessary from Broad, really. He bowls a fuller ball on middle and off, Marsh bunts it back towards him. He crouches low in his followthrough and reverse flicks it at the striker's end. The ball deflects off the stumps and goes towards the right of the keeper. Smith is aware and he steals a brisk single. Bairstow had a shy at the bowler's end but he missed the target.
Fuller on the stumps, worked towards mid-wicket.
Fuller in the zone outside off, driven sweetly again but finds the man at cover.

FOUR! Superb batting! Second boundary of the over! He goes past 500 runs in the Ashes this year. Anderson drops it short on middle, not much venom behind it. Smith pulls it neatly and the man at long leg could do nothing about it. Steven is on the move.
Fuller on off, blocked solidly.

FOUR! There he goes! Delightful from Smith! Anderson bowls it around off, Smith takes it from there as he gets across a touch and then his wrists do the rest. Beats the dive of the fielder at square leg and picks up his first boundary of the day.

Off the inner half! Fuller in length, right up there and Smith is into the drive. He looks to go with the shot but gets a thick inside edge towards mid on. The Aussie skipper is clearly annoyed with himself. He wanted to win the battle here.
Good length ball outside off, holding its line, Smith is happy to make a leave.
A silly mid off for Smith and a catching cover as well. Expect Anderson to pitch it right up there.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Shorter in length and outside off, Marsh dabs it towards backward point.
Shaun Marsh and Steven Smith are happy to play the dot balls. They are in no hurry to score this morning. Doing a sensible job of seeing off the new ball, getting the hang of the pace on the pitch...
Angling away from the southpaw, Marsh pats it with soft hands towards cover. Looks to cross but Smith isn't too keen on it.
Good length on middle and off, defended towards cover off the back foot.

Good timing! Slightly fuller and angling away outside off, Marsh leans ahead and sweetly times it through cover. Was in the air for a while but in the gap as well. Two taken and it's 250 up for Australia.
Broad goes over the wicket to Marsh now! He hurls it on a length around middle and off, defended from within the crease towards mid on.
Giving nothing away! Bowling according to the field given. Fuller ball on off, Smith leans forward to push it straight to mid off.
Marginally short, in the channel on off, punched towards mid off.
Back to fuller length, pushed off the middle of the bat towards the off side.
Some good intensity there! Hits the deck hard, gets the extra bounce and Smith turns his head out of the way to leave it alone.
Good line and length from Jimmy! Keeps it a touch fuller on off, Smith takes a stride forward and blocks it towards cover again.
Anderson drops it on a back of a length outside off, Smith punches it off the back foot towards cover.
Good length delivery on off, clipped towards mid-wicket for nothing.
Bangs in a short one but it doesn't rise much, Steven Smith swivels and rolls his wrists to get it towards Moeen Ali at fine leg for a single. All along the ground.
Short and angling down leg, Smith moves inside the line to let Bairstow do some work.
Pitches it up on off, Smith presses ahead and drives it beautifully but finds Malan stationed at short cover.
Good length delivery on off, Smith moves across and defends it down.
Nice soft hands! Smith gets across to this back of a length delivery and tucks it through backward square leg to bag a couple.
Back of a length delivery around middle and leg, tucked towards mid-wicket comfortably. A maiden to start with for Anderson.
Keeps it on a fuller length on the stumps, Marsh looks to drive it away on the off side but the bat turns in his hands and as a result, he gets it off the inner half towards mid on.
Slants it away on a fuller length, Shaun with a front foot push towards backward point.
Fuller on the pads, worked towards mid-wicket by coming across.
Shortish length delivery, angling away outside off, Marsh with an open face bat pushes it towards backward point.
Good length delivery, on middle and off, Marsh presses forward and defends it towards cover.
James Anderson to have a go from the other end.
Sprayed wider outside off, Steven Smith makes a watchful leave.
Good line! A bit fuller and just outside off, Smith makes an easy leave.
Good shot! See the confidence. Pitches it up on off, Smith leans forward and square drives it neatly but it goes straight towards backward point.
A bit too straight from Stuart. Easily clipped through backward square leg for a single. First run of the day.

A huge shout for an LBW! Maybe, a bit too high. Broad angles it in from around off, it zips a bit as Marsh misses his attempted flick shot. The ball hits his pads and goes towards the off side. Broad appeals for an LBW but nothing from the umpire.
Right on the money is Broad! Starts from round the wicket and angles it pretty full on middle. Shaun Marsh is quick to get his bat down and keep it out back towards the left of the bowler.

It's time to get rolling. The players and umpires have made their way out to the middle. The crowd is brimming in anticipation as the two overnight batsmen, Steven Smith and Shaun Marsh walk out. Bill Lawry in the commentary box, what better than hearing him out. Stuart Broad will be the one to steam in first up. Two slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

England need to take wickets and that too quickly this morning to get back into the game. Not that they are out of it, but if they don't come up with plans, they might very well be. Their spearheads, Anderson and Broad will be looking to make the most of the new cherry. If they manage to remove the Aussie skipper early, things could turn in their favour. Stay with us to see how the day pans out...

Hello and a warm welcome for the second day of the MCG Test. Australia are in a fairly good position after Steven Smith opted to bat. Warner got them off to a flier and then with a bit of trouble in the middle, their skipper steadied the ship, just what he is good at. Shaun Marsh has given him good company until now and the duo's unbeaten stand is worth 84. Should they continue to dig in there, it wouldn't be wrong to predict, they will be well on course to post a big first innings total.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Just before the close of play, Root opted to take the second new ball and Anderson and Broad bowled exceedingly well sans any success. We saw that once the ball became softer, run-scoring became difficult but when it was hard and new, it was coming on the bat nicely. So, the new cherry is just 20 balls old and it would be interesting to see if England can come out tomorrow morning and make it count, should they fail, the hosts will just run away with the game. They would be looking to bat once and bat big and with their skipper once again at it, the signs are ominous for England. On that note, we take your leave but do join us tomorrow at 1030 Local (2330 GMT, previous day) to catch all the action from day 2 of the MCG Test. Until then, it's goodbye from us. Cheers!

It was Woakes who provided his side the first breakthrough. The visitors were right on the money in the middle session as they scalped two wickets and dried up the runs completely, giving away just 43 in that period. Come the final session, all eyes were on the English bowlers who had their tails up but, as has been the case in the series, Steven Smith arrived to the occasion to bail his side out of the stutter, scoring a fluent half century. Shaun Marsh, who could have gotten out on his very first ball, played a perfect foil to his skipper to keep the scoreboard moving. The duo stitched an unbeaten 84-run stand and made sure that there was no more hiccup.

Excellent session for Australia and they end the day on a high. Having won the toss and opting to bat on a flat deck, David Warner was up and running from the word go. He along with Cameron Bancroft scored 102 runs in the first session to make the most of the conditions on offer. The southpaw scored a breezy century, although he got a life when he was on 99. However, both of them departed in quick succession and it seemed like England have got the opening they needed.
Fuller in length and angling in from around off, Steven Smith gets behind the line and offers a straight bat to see off the day. STUMPS ON DAY 1!
Ahead of a length and served outside off, nicely defended off the back foot.
Fuller and attacking the stumps, Smith gets across and drives it straight to mid on.
Anderson bowls it a tad short outside off, Smith with a bit of shuffle, defends it down on the track.
Hurls it in the corridor of uncertainty, Steven makes a watchful leave.
Drops it on a length and this one bounces a bit more as Smith defends it towards cover off the back foot.
Jimmy Anderson to bowl the final over of the day! Can he pick up a wicket?
Fuller outside off, Shaun Marsh is solid in his front foot defense.
Broad angles it in from outside off, it's on a back of a length. Marsh defends it back down the track.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Angles it on a fuller length on the pads, Marsh flicks it neatly but finds mid-wicket.
Good shape on this one but it's too wide outside off to make the batsman play at it.
Fuller and angling in on middle and leg, Smith shuffles a bit and pushes it wide of mid on for a quick single.
Beautiful bowling from Anderson! This one shapes away a touch, but the line is around off which forces Shaun to play at it. Just about whizzes past the outside edge. Excellent from Jimmy.
Pitches it up on middle and leg, clipped straight to mid-wicket for nothing.
A bit short and around off, Marsh stands tall and defends it down.
Fuller and angling in on the pads, too easy for Smith as he flicks it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Good length around off, Smith comes forward and blocks it out towards cover.

A peach to begin with! When the ball is doing something, Jimmy Anderson is the best option to go to. He steams in from over the wicket and angles it in from around off. Smith comes forward to play inside the line but this one shapes away a bit and nearly kisses the outside edge of his bat. Hands on head for Anderson.
James Anderson to share the new ball with Broad.
Almost! Short and outside off, Marsh sans any feet movement tries to go after it and gets beaten all ends up.
On a length and just around off, Marsh gets squared up a touch as he pushes it towards cover.
A delay here as England have decided to take the second new ball. Will the new cherry help them take a wicket?
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good length on the fifth stump line, Marsh blocks it towards cover.
Fuller and veering on the pads, Marsh moves inside the line to help it on its way but misses. Bairstow does well to dive to his right to collect it.
Broad from around the wicket, drops it short on off. Marsh looks to cut it but it's too close to do so. Chops it on the bounce towards gully.
With 16 minutes to go and 5 overs remaining in the day, when will England take the second new ball? Anyway, it is Stuart Broad who is brought into the attack.
Fuller on off, a nice front foot defense on offer from SS.
Fuller on the stumps, it's the slower one. Marsh looks to drive but squirts it off the inner half through backward square leg for a single.
Back of a length outside off, patted towards point for one.

FOUR! Not intentional but gets the desired result! Curran bowls it full and wide outside off, too much of width and Steven Smith decides to go after it. He looks to guide it down but gets it off the outer half wide of the gully fielder for a boundary towards third man. No one in the deep, so it's easy pickings for him.
Good length delivery, angling in on middle, a bit of shuffle from Smith as he defends it towards mid on.
Another off pace delivery from Curran around off. Smith reads it well and dead-bats it.
Aggression from Woakes! Bowls an overpitched delivery and Marsh drives it hard back to him. He collects it and mimes a throw to the keeper's end.
Almost a replica of the previous delivery as Marsh lunges ahead in defense.
Attacks the stumps with a full length ball, Marsh comes forward and defends it with his bat close to the pad.
Shortish delivery, Smith helps it around the corner for a run.
Back of a length ball, shaping in. Smith walks across his sticks and nudges it towards mid-wicket.
In the corridor outside off, Smith covers his stumps to allow it through.
Serves it on a length, the fifth stump line, easy leave for SM.
Another slower delivery, it's a bit too wayward from Curran. Down the leg side as Smith waits for the ball to come and then tickles it towards fine leg for a single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Once again the slower one from Curran! Almost in every over he seems to be bowling one. The back of the hand delivery, again the length is short which gives Smith all the time in the world to go back and defend it down.
Shortish and outside off, tapped towards the left of the point fielder for a brisk single.
On a length and angling in on middle and leg, glanced down towards backward square leg for a single.

Another boundary ball and Marsh misses out. He knows he has missed out on that one! Woakes serves it short and wide outside off, Marsh cuts it nicely off the back foot but finds Ali at backward point.
FOUR! Delightful from Marshy! A bit too full outside off, right in the slot for the southpaw. Shaun leans into it and caresses it through cover. Into the gap and away she whistles to the ropes.
Fuller on middle, wirsted towards mid on.
Back of a length, angling in from outside off. Shaun Marsh stays put as he tries to cut but it's too close to get going. Ends up chopping it towards gully.
Back of a length outside off, punched towards short cover off the back foot.
Full and attacking the stumps. Woakes angles it in but Marsh is quick to get across and work it with soft hands towards mid-wicket.
Hurls it wider outside off, the Aussie skipper has got nothing to do with that one.
Stays perfectly behind the line to stab it out.
Comes over the wicket for Smith and bowls the leg cutter. Gets it to bounce a bit more but it's on the shorter length which gives the Aussie skipper enough time to rock back and keep it out.
Shortish again and served outside off, Shaun opens the face of the bat and times it towards backward point where Woakes dives to makes a half stop. The batsmen take a single.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Shaun Marsh taps it towards the cover-point fielder.
Too straight from Curran to start the spell! Smith walks across and clips it down to fine leg for a single.
The second new ball is available but it has not been taken. There is a change in bowling. Curran comes back for a bowl.
Comes from around the wicket, keeps it full on off, Marsh prods forward in defense.
Drifts on the pads, Smith tucks it down to fine leg for a single.
Fuller again on the stumps, Smith walks across to play the on drive but gets it off the toe end towards mid on.
Fuller and angling in on middle, Smith gets across to bunt it towards mid on.
This one stays low! It's on a length around middle and off, Steven crouches low and somehow manages to keep it out.
Good length delivery, angling in, Smith gets across and defends it down watchfully.
Smith drives it wide of the man at mid on to keep strike.
Skips down the track and whips it towards mid on. The man there fumbles which allows them to take the single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! That's a rare mistake from Malan! He drops it short on middle, Marsh has ample time to rock back and pull it. He does so in front of square on the leg side. There were two men in the deep but he bisected them to perfection.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter one around leg, Smith flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Fuller outside off, driven towards the cover-point fielder.

Short and angling in on middle, Shaun Marsh once again goes for the pull but this one doesn't rise much and as a result he gets hit on the box. An appeal has been made which is turned down immediately by the umpire.
Stands back and punches it towards cover.
Just short of the man at mid-wicket! A bit short around middle and off, Marsh swivels to pull but doesn't bother to keep it down. Almost spoons a catch to the man at short mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery, angling in, defended towards the point fielder.
Chris Woakes is brought back into the attack.

There it is! Steven Smith and his good run of form continues. Leans forward to this flighted delivery and drives it through extra cover to come back for the second. 22nd Test fifty for the Aussie skipper! There is no stopping him. Remember, he has a sore bottom hand but still he has delivered for his side. Another big one on the cards? Well, looks like.
Flatter around middle and leg, clipped off the back foot towards square leg.
The batsman charges down the wicket. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Leans across and with the turn, whips it towards mid-wicket.

Off the splice! Bowls the googly, it bounces a touch more as Marsh looks to defend it off the front foot. Is undone by it as the ball hits the splice of the bat and dies down in the vacant short leg region.

Drifting in from around middle and leg, a bit short which allows Marsh to flick it away towards deep mid-wicket. There is a bit of hesitation between the two but they complete the second run easily in the end.

This one curls back in from a good length, Smith shuffles across the sticks and defends it off the inner half towards mid on. Just 17 runs coming in the last 10 overs for Australia. Good thing from England is that, they haven't allowed the hosts to score freely.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Shortish and outside off, Steven goes back and defends it towards the point fielder.
Fuller and outside off, driven through cover-point for a single.

Beaten! This is superb from Jimmy Anderson! First he angles it in from around off, makes the batsman draw forward and then gets it to straighten away to leave him stranded. Just whizzes past the outside edge!
Fuller ball on off, Shaun Marsh leans forward only to find Root at short cover.

Flatter one around middle and leg, Smith goes back and clips it but is unable to beat the man at square leg. A maiden from Malan, tidy stuff from the leggie. He hasn't allowed the pair to score freely, something that Ali was lacking considerably.
A low full toss around middle, Smith whips this one but Curran at square leg makes a diving stop.
Slower one, but it's too full on the stumps. SS jams it out towards mid on.
Flatter delivery on middle, clipped towards backward square leg. Wants the single but won't get it. Stays on 49!
Flighted delivery around middle and off, the Aussie skipper, with a stride forward defends it back to Malan.
Loopy ball around middle and leg, flicked towards mid-wicket for nothing.
Goes wide of the crease and angles it away a touch, SM defends it safely towards point.
Now brings one back into the southpaw, Marsh waits for it before bunting it to mid on.
Nice inswingers and outswingers from Anderson at the moment. This time he gets it to move away, Marsh leans across and drives it but finds the man at short cover.
Fuller in length and curling back in a touch, defended off the front foot with a solid straight bat.
Good length delivery on the stumps, Shaun prods ahead and with his bat close to the pad, he works it towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery, angling away, Marsh punches it off the back foot towards cover.
Slows it through the air, but it's on the shorter side, Steven clips it towards backward square leg.
Quicker through the air on middle, Smith hangs back to punch it towards mid-wicket.
Gets down the track and whips it towards short mid-wicket.
Floated delivery on off, Smith takes a stride forward and eases it through extra cover to collect a couple. Moves to 49 with that!
Tossed up outside off, pushed off the front foot towards point.
Flattish around leg, Smith goes back to clip it away but gets hit on the pads.

Pitches it up outside off, Smith leans into it and drives it towards extra cover for a single. This also brings up the 50-run stand. Once again when England were threatening to chip away at the wickets, a good partnership from the hosts have denied them.
Walks across even before the bowler comes and then drives it towards mid on.
Hurls in a length ball and this one nips back in a touch, Steven Smith walks across the stumps and makes another assured leave.
On a length and outside off, Smith makes an easy leave. This one stayed a touch low as well.
Fuller in length and outside off, Steven leans forward and just checks his drive as the ball rolls towards point.
Starts off with a length delivery, a bit wide outside off from over the wicket, Smith stabs it towards cover.

Time for Drinks. England kicked off the final session nicely as Broad got the ball to reverse. He caught Khawaja napping and almost dismissed Marsh in his first delivery. However, Steven Smith played freely from the word go and pulled back the initiative. He hasn't been dismissed at the MCG yet and has an average well over 100. Ominous signs for the visitors. Marsh has also grown in confidence and is playing sensibly. The Englishmen need a breakthrough, especially of the Australian skipper.
Quicker one this time, skidding through. Marsh makes good use of the depth of the crease to stonewall it.
Floated outside off, Shaun chips down the track and strokes it to mid off.
On a flatter trajectory around off, dealt with nicely off the back foot.
A fraction short this time, tucked through square leg for a run.
Fullish delivery, played with soft hands to mid off.
Tossed up delivery, Smith lunges forward in defense.
An off pace yorker on middle, Marsh is equal to the task as he jams it out. Another good over from Curran.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Curran goes for a slower ball again but sprays it down the leg side. Marsh misses his glance.
In the corridor outside off, left alone.

Short delivery on middle and leg, Smith helps his pull down to fine leg for a single. On a couple of occasions in Perth, Smith got hit on the back of the hand while attempting a pull shot. This time he had it covered.
FOUR! Great stroke! Shortish delivery outside off and a bit of room on offer. Smith rises with the bounce and steers it through the point region to pick up another boundary.
Floated outside off, defended solidly off the front foot.
A bit short on middle, blocked off the back foot.
Drifting in on middle, tucked around the corner for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Wider outside off, pushed off the front foot to covers.
Full on middle, played off the inner half of the bat to mid on.
Full ball outside off, jammed out to covers.

Shane Warne on air gives us a good insight about Tom Curran. He explains that he bowls his cutters with no change in his action. That is why those change of paces are so effective. It has got him wickets in the shorter formats of the game, will be interesting to see if it works here...
In the channel outside off, left alone.
This fullish ball is clipped to the leg side for a single.
Back of the hand delivery, almost deceiving Smith. The batsman shapes for a drive but adjusts well to keep it out.

A chirpy appeal for an LBW is turned down. Full length ball, angling down leg. Marsh tries to clip it away but gets hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards square leg as the umpire turns the appeal down. A leg bye taken.
Good length ball, shaping in from outside off. Marsh shuffles a touch and defends it solidly.
Full again, whipped to the man at short mid-wicket.
Wrong one from Malan. It is full on middle, Marsh reads it well and clips it towards wide mid on for a single. 200 up for Australia. The MCG crowd appreciates that.

Shoddy stuff from James Vince! Tossed up around off, Marsh drives it towards deepish mid off and takes on Vince. The fielder is lazy to get across to his left and makes a mess of it. Concedes a couple.
Marsh drives the fullish delivery nicely but fails to pierce the gap as the man at extra cover stops it.
Hangs back to the flatter delivery and dead-bats it.
Short on middle and leg, clipped through square leg for a single.

Dawid Malan to roll his arm over now. He bowled better than Moeen Ali in Perth. Not sure this is the correct decision though. These two are good players of spin and this might allow them to run away with the show.
He hasn't been able to execute his drives properly today. Fullish ball outside off, Marsh goes at it with hard hands but gets an inside edge to mid on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On a length around off, angling in. Marsh has it covered as he keeps it out with a straight bat.
Shuffles across to the full length ball on middle and leg and works it through square leg for a run.
Fuller in length, blocked nicely.
Good fielding! Fractionally overpitched outside off, Smith strokes it nicely but Malan dives to his right to make a nice stop.

Steven Smith and Shaun Marsh are showing urgency in the middle. They are being helped by the fact that Joe Root is sticking with Moeen Ali. No real turn on offer and the duo is picking him off with ease. Will be a good ploy to bring pacers from both ends with the ball reversing.
Leans ahead and defends this one with his bat close to the pad.
Drifting in towards Smith who eases it to mid on to get off strike.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Marsh is growing in confidence. Gets a full ball on middle and clips it beautifully through mid on for a boundary.
Leans forward and strokes it through covers for a single.
Fullish on middle and leg, turned around the corner for a single.
Ooh.. substantial movement again! Curves back in sharply from a length outside off, Smith covers the line, tries to keep it out but gets an inside edge onto his pads.

Where did that come from? Curran opts for a leg-cutter and bowls it on a length in the corridor outside off. Smith gets foxed but does well in the end to drops his wrists and play it along the ground towards the slip region.
Plays this fullish ball to covers and tells his partner to wait on.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Michael Clarke on air praises Steven Smith. He explains that no team hasn't been able to found out a certain plan against him. He is good with his drives. Whenever the bowler feels that he has a chance by curving the ball in on the stumps, he is ready to pounce on them. Though he moves around a lot in his crease, his head position is always balanced and his good hand-eye co-ordination works in his favour. An absolute treat to watch!
Back of a length outside off, Steven pats it to the off side.
Full length delivery, Smith shuffles and jams it to extra cover.
Tossed up delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.
FOUR! Nicely done! A fraction short this time, spinning away. Marsh rocks back and cuts it past the point fielder for a boundary. He found the gap to perfection. This stroke will calm his nerves.
Marsh also uses his feet and drives it to mid on but no single on offer this time.
Smith is nimble on his feet as he clips it to mid on and calls his partner through for a swift single.
Short and room on offer, flayed away through point for a brace.
Spinning in slowly from outside off, blocked nicely off the back foot.
Slower delivery from Curran. Smith reads it well and tucks it around the corner for a run.
On a length, extra bounce on offer. Marsh rises up and plays it to gully for a single.
Curran is bending his back. Steams in and angles in a good length ball. Marsh is late to bring his bat down and gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Overpitched outside off, driven crisply but straight to extra cover.
Curran goes wide of the crease and brings it in, Marsh taps it with an open bat face to point.
Back of a length delivery, swinging in. Smith hangs back and taps it to mid on for a run. There is movement in the air for Curran as well.
Tom Curran is back for a burst. He has been good so far. Not sure this is the right decision though. Stuart Broad was getting good reverse swing and Joe Root should have stuck with him for a while.
A bit flatter outside off, defended from within the crease.
Fullish around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Man at deep cover coming up. A slip and a short leg also in place for Marsh. The umpire is having a  chat with Moeen Ali. He conveys to him that the ball tracking is not working at the moment.
Shortish ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, Smith shuffles a long way across and dead-bats it.
Length delivery outside off, kept out nicely.

FOUR! Sublime! Tossed up outside off, Smith strides forward confidently and strokes it through extra cover. The fielder in the deep covers a lot of ground to his right, slides but fails to keep the ball in play. The skipper is going from strength-to-strength.
Moeen Ali returns for a bowl.
Another false shot. Full ball outside off, swinging in. Marsh goes for a drive without any foot movement and gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Eases the full ball through covers for a single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Poor stuff from Marsh! He is looking fidgety. On a drivable length outside off, Shaun goes for an expansive drive with no feet movement and gets an inside edge past the leg stump. A run taken.
He is so easy on the eye with his drives. Gets a pitched up delivery in his arc and creams it through covers. Another three taken.
Full length ball outside off, left alone.
Woakes goes around the wicket to Marsh and angles it in. Marsh covers the line to keep it out.
On a drivable length outside off, Smith leans into it and drives it nicely through covers. Three runs taken.
Back of a length this time, blocked nicely.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

FOUR! Brilliantly played! Fullish delivery, Smith shuffles a touch and clips it in the gap between the two short mid-wicket fielders and picks up another boundary. Smith becomes the leading run-scorer in Tests in 2017. The best Test batsman in the world keeps on getting better and better.
Full delivery, swerving in, blocked solidly.
Full length ball, tailing in substantially. Marsh does well to jam it to mid-wicket. What an over from Broad, a wicket-maiden.
Short of a length outside off, left alone.
Fuller in length, kept out watchfully.

Another huge appeal! It is all happening at the MCG. The ball is reversing for Broad and Marsh doesn't have any clue about it. Broad bowls a full delivery on middle and leg, Marsh loses his balance as he tries to flick it away and gets hit on the pads. England go up in unison but umpire S Ravi once again stays unmoved. The on-air commentators reckon that it is going down the leg side. Broad looks at his skipper but this time he doesn't go for the review. Sensible call as Hawk Eye shows that the ball was missing the leg stump.

Not Out! Shaun Marsh survives a tough call but England do not lose a review. Length delivery around off, jagging back appreciably. Marsh is caught in the crease as he attempts to clip it away but misses to get pinged on the pads. England roar in appeal but umpire S Ravi stays unmoved. Broad walks to his skipper and convinces him to go for the review. The body language from the visitors is really confident. Time for the replays. The impact is in line but it is just clipping the top of the stumps. Hence, the umpire's call stays.
England on the charge. They reckon that they have trapped Shaun Marsh in front of the stumps and go for the review. Big moment in the game. Height might be a factor.
Shaun Marsh strides out to bat.

OUT! Soft dismissal! Khawaja never looked at ease throughout his knock and has finally perished. Broad steams in from around the wicket and bowls it on a good length in the zone of apprehension. The ball is holding its line as Khawaja pokes at it tamely. Ends up getting a feather and Bairstow accepts it gleefully. Bowling in the corridor has worked wonders for the visitors. Is this the opening England needed?
FOUR! Timing and placement, brilliantly played! Short of a length outside off, Smith waits for it and places it deftly past point for a boundary.

In the air... but safe! In the channel around off, straightens after pitching. Smith gets squared up and gets an outside edge but the ball falls well short of the gully fielder. Playing that with soft hands saved him.
Back of a length ball on off, Steven hangs back and offers a straight bat in defense.
Continues to probe in that off stump channel. Smith is equal to the task as he shuffles across and blocks it with a straight bat.
Similar length ball around off, Smith shuffles across in his customary manner and defends it solidly.
A good shot for no runs! Shortish delivery and room on offer, Smith punches it beautifully but finds the man at point.
On a drivable length outside off, Khawaja doesn't fall for the bait and defends it off the front foot.
Shortens his length, Usman hangs back and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Once again nails the drive to the cover region but picks up the man this time.
FOUR! Elegant! This will give Khawaja confidence. Half volley outside off, the batsman leans ahead and creams it through extra cover for a glorious boundary.
Back of a length around off, Khawaja hops back and blocks it stoutly.
Straying on the pads, clipped in front of square leg for a brace. He needs to keep on rotating strike.
Stuart Broad to bowl from the other end.
Shuffles across to the good length delivery and pushes it to mid on.
That was tentative! On a length outside off, straightens after hitting the deck. Smith goes at it half-heartedly and gets beaten all ends up.
Mitchell Starc on-air reckons that the pitch slowed in the second session as opposed to the morning session when the ball was coming on to the bat. Feels that is why the batsmen slowed down.
Shorter in length around off, defended solidly off the back foot.
Fuller in length, Smith covers the line to block it.

Another brilliant observation. This time from Ian Healy. He notices that Khawaja played a full-blooded pull shot somewhere in the second session which went only for a single. Similar ball, similar length. What does Smith get? A boundary. No change in field from that ball to this. So how does Smith get a boundary? Because he knows where the fielders are placed. So the key to playing your pull shots is - not every time power is needed. Khawaja instantaneously goes for power on the pull, but does not focus much on placement. Smith well, mixes the two really well.
FOUR! Shot! Shortish delivery on middle and leg, Smith gets on top of the bounce and pulls it with aplomb through backward square leg to find the fence.
Starts off with a good length ball on middle and leg, Khawaja tucks it to fine leg to rotate strike.
We are back for the final session. Steven Smith and Usman Khawaja will continue their innings. Chris Woakes will continue his spell.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

Drama happened when David Warner was on 99. The debutant, Tom Curran was the culprit as he overstepped and that meant that the opener who got caught at mid on lived on. He did score a ton and was applauded deservedly from the MCG crowd. However, he got dismissed soon after to some smart bowling from Anderson. England need to continue the good work while the hosts will be expecting their skipper, Steven Smith to rise to the occasion again. Join us for the final session in a while.

A great session for England as they have picked up two wickets and only conceded 43 runs. After struggling to bowl well in the first session, they have bounced back in style. They have bowled tight lines and lengths to stifle the hosts. It was Chris Woakes who broke the flourishing opening stand to send Bancroft back. Usman Khawaja came in but failed to rotate strike. He went in to his shell and as a result, Warner also got bogged down a bit.
Wide outside off to end the over and session, Smith lets it through. TEA ON DAY 1!
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Landed pretty wide outside off, left alone.

That is a jaffa. Broad is surprised too. Sums up his bowling in this match so far. He has just been bowling wide, trying to make the batsmen commit a mistake. But here, he makes Smith play at a good delivery and that ball just jags back in, whizzing past the outside edge. Broad gives a stare at Smith and awaits a reaction but Smith is just like a monk who only gives blessings with no trouble in the world. Only the smile was missing there.
Landed outside off, Smith gets across and defends.
Down the leg side, tucked behind square leg for a single. Reckon he won't come back on strike for the rest of this over...
Shortish on middle, Smith gets across and defends it back down the track.
Again it's on a fuller length outside off, Steven presses forward and drives it towards short cover.
Fuller and around off, Steven Smith gets across and works it towards mid-wicket.
Fuller and angling in on middle and leg, clipped towards square leg.
Full and outside off, Smith leans forward and square drives it towards the point fielder.
Fuller and angling in from around off, defends it towards the cover fielder.

Good observation from Ian Chappell on air, as always. Priceless commentary. He looks at the bottom hand grip of Khawaja and reckons it is a pretty strong hold. Normally, he says, when you observe strong bottom-handed players, they keep it very tight when playing square of the wicket but when it comes to playing a cover drive or down the ground, they loosen it a touch. But not Usman. He keeps that grip very tight almost throughout. Now look at the way Steven Smith bats. He too, bats with a very strong bottom-handed grip. But then he loosens it a touch if he is playing a shot down the ground. Adding further, Chappell says that most batsmen who play for New South Wales have a strong bottom-handed grip. Khawaja is from Queesland but then shifted to NSW.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Takes a stride forward and drives it towards cover.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Good length ball on middle, Khawaja shows full face of the bat.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fuller in length and outside off, driven through covers for a single.

Stuart Broad is back on. Australia's run rate has come down considerably after the first session. Tells you that the Englishmen has comeback hard but Khawaja has also been in his shell which has made life difficult for the hosts.
Fullish delivery, patted to mid on.
Overpitched outside off, Khawaja drives it towards covers where the fielder dives to his right to make a good stop. No easy runs for the southpaw.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Short ball on middle and leg, you can't bowl there with no fine leg in place. Khawaja stands tall and pulls it through the same region to find the fence.
Well played! Fractionally overpitched outside off, Smith leans into it and strokes it through covers. The fielder from the same region chases it and saves a run for his side.
Fuller length ball outside off, Smith mistimes his drive to mid off.
Chris Woakes returns for a burst. He was poor to begin with but was good in his second spell. Can he continue the good work?
Shorter in length, tucked around the corner for a single.
Back of a length outside off, Smith dabs it to the point region.
Back of a length on middle and leg, Smith hops and fends it off to square leg.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Fuller in length, Smith shuffles across and clips it to mid-wicket.
On a length and angling in, kept out nicely.
Leg slip in place now. Interesting tactic from the Englishmen.
Pounds the deck hard around off, Khawaja hops and blocks it. He is getting bogged down, needs to find a way to rotate the strike.
In the zone outside off, Usman offers a solid back foot defense.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Back of a length around off, played off the back foot to the off side.
Full length ball outside off, driven with hard hands to covers.
Good length ball around off, defended off the back foot.
Fuller in length, kept out watchfully. End of a productive over.
Hangs back to the good length delivery and blocks it.
Steven Smith is the next batsman in.

OUT! The best bowler in the English side strikes! This is what happens when you bowl closer to the stumps. Yes, England have dried down the runs by bowling wide lines but you cannot keep doing that for a lifetime. That is the difference between Broad and Anderson. The former was just testing the patience of the batsmen but Jimmy, boy, he played with their minds. Intelligent bowling from the experienced campaigner and he reaps the dividends. After bowling a couple of back of length deliveries, he goes back to a fullish ball. He hurls it in the channel outside off, angling in initially. But then the ball deviates away just a shade. Warner with minimal foot movement pokes at it and gets a faint nick. Jonny Bairstow  behind the stumps takes a regulation catch and throws the ball up in the air. Anderson is confident as well and up goes the umpire's finger. Warner is not too sure and thinks about the review. He walks down the track and has a chat with Khawaja but that conversation takes ages. Eventually, he just about starts to make that signal for a 'T' but the umpire says - 'Sorry mate. You are timed out.' The umpires check for the front foot no ball and importantly for England, it is fine this time. The opener walks back to a warm reception from the crowd after playing a brilliant knock. Perhaps, Khawaja's inability to rotate the strike bogged Warner down. Consider this - In this partnership, David just managed 7 from 39 balls. Ouch. This is also Anderson's 100th Test wicket against Australia, a record to be proud of. Good passage of play for England. Now can they get another wicket before Tea?
Back of a length around off, David covers the line and eases it to covers.
Anderson drags his length back. Bowls a shortish delivery, Warner goes deep in the crease and defends it solidly.
Fullish in length, angling in. Warner hangs back and makes an assured leave.
Overpitched outside off, driven sweetly to mid off.
In the corridor of uncertainty again, Khawaja lets it go. Intent has been missing from the No. 3. With Australia on the front foot, he needs to play positive cricket.
Length delivery in the zone of apprehension, Khawaja comes forward confidently and blocks it.
Shortish delivery around off, Usman hangs back and taps it to covers .
Back of a length around off, defended solidly off the back foot.
That's a beautiful delivery! Fuller in length outside off, straightens after hitting the deck. Khawaja pokes at it but is beaten all ends up.
This is wide outside off and Warner doesn't fiddle with it.
Back of a length outside off, Warner hangs back and stonewalls it.
Nicely bowled! Slower ball on a full length outside off, Warner shapes for a booming drive but only jams it out in the end towards covers.
Overpitched outside off, driven sweetly to the cover region.

Good point mentioned by the on-air commentators. There is a sweeper cover in place for Warner and the bowlers are bowling according to the field. So, it becomes difficult for Warner to score boundaries. Khawaja hasn't rotated the strike much. He needs to take initiative and keep the scoreboard ticking.
On a length on off, David remains in crease and plays it with soft hands towards mid on.
Good length ball outside off, Warner hangs back and taps it with an open bat face to cover-point.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, Khawaja puts his head down and defends it calmly.
Short and width on offer, cut away through point for a run.
Fuller in length on middle and leg, Khawaja looks to turn it to the leg side but gets a safe leading edge towards the non-striker.
Fuller in length, driven off the front foot to mid on.
It's been driven superbly through the covers. One run added to the total.
Back of a length ball, punched off the back foot to extra cover.
Shortish and served outside off, Khawaja doesn't bother going after it. Back-to-back maidens!
Back of a length delivery on middle, tucked towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Length delivery, coming back in a shade, Khawaja drives it to the man at mid off.
Just a lean forward and driven towards the short cover fielder.
Pitches it in that zone outside off, Khawaja has got nothing to do with that one.
Good length delivery, angling in from outside off, Usman Khawaja prods forward and defends it with his bat and pad close together.
Fuller in the zone outside off, David Warner drives it towards the man at extra cover. A maiden from Tom Curran!
Leans forward and eases the drive towards short cover.
Shortish and outside off, Warner hops back to defend and in doing so, his bottom hand comes off as well.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Ahead of a length and around off, defended towards the man at short cover.
What a delivery! Absolute peach from Curran! He brings this one in from around off and then straightens a bit to nearly take the outside edge of Warner's bat.
Shortish outside off, Usman once again offers no shot.
Angles it in from around off, Khawaja knows where his off stump is and then makes a leave. Three leaves in a low.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Outside off, UK makes an easy leave.
Fuller outside off, Warner drives it uppishly through covers for a single.
Gets forward and pushes it towards cover.
Drinks time.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

David Warner gets to his ton! And the typical celebrations follow! He lets out a huge roar, leaps in the air and then punches his fist in joy. Phew! Would have departed on 99 on the previous ball but there is something called as lady luck and David Warner had her right behind him. The crowd is up on its feet and David Warner takes a moment to sink in all the applause. It took him around 40-odd minutes to get to the milestone after being in the 90s. Length delivery on middle and off, he tucks it through square leg and sprints to the other end in joy. Well played, Sir.

CURRAN HAS OVERSTEPPED! All the celebrations have been cut short and the MCG crowd is loving it. How often do you get to see this? A batsman getting a reprieve just one short of a ton. Got to feel for the debutant here but he has only himself to blame. Tom Curran bowls it on a length around off, Warner looks to half-pull this one but the ball bounces a touch more which means a leading edge is induced. The ball lobs up towards Broad at mid on who takes the catch. But the umpire asks Warner to wait as he wants to check the front foot. Guess what? Tom Curran is well ahead of the popping line. Worked so hard for it, the ideal wicket to have, but it's all gone for a toss. Deary me... David Warner survives on 99. Can he make the Englishmen pay or will something more dramatic happen here now?
Goodness me! Warner has been caught on 99, would you believe? But the umpire has asked him to wait as he wants to check Curran's front foot. This seems to be a life for Warner...
Back of a length around middle and off, Warner tucks it uppishly towards mid on. The crowd is right behind him.
Bowls it slower this time, at 112.6 kph, Warner waits and just pushes it towards short cover.
Shortish and angling in. Khawaja pulls it through backward square leg to bring Warner back on strike.
In the channel outside off, UK leaves it alone.
Tom Curran is back on.
Fuller on off, Warner drives it towards cover but couldn't get it past the man there.
Too straight from Anderson, Khawaja turns it through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Fuller and angling in, Usman defends it down.
On a length and around middle and off, Khawaja defends.

Punches it through the cover, moves to 99! He achieves a milestone. 6000 Test runs for him! Amazing feat! Back of a length outside off, Warner punches by getting on top it through cover. Wants two but Moeen Ali in the deep is quick to the ball.
James Anderson who wasn't allowed to bowl is now given the permission.
A bit shorter in length, in line of the stumps. Usman camps back and defends it stoutly.
Good length ball around off, Usman covers the line and defends it stoutly.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Good length ball in the zone of apprehension, Khawaja doesn't fiddle with it.
Overpitched on middle and leg, nudged nicely through wide mid on for a couple.
On a length around off, Khawaja stays back and defends it calmly.
Overpitched outside off, Warner drives it nicely but finds the man at extra cover.
Warner flays this one hard but finds the man at short cover-point.

Uppish but safe! Warner must have had his heart in his mouth. Short and width on offer, Warner goes for a full-blooded cut and plays it uppishly towards backward point. The fielder dives full length to his right but the ball goes past him in a flash. Ali in the deep does the mopping up job to keep it down to a couple. Warner moves to 98, the crowd cheers for him loudly. He was stranded on 96 for 9 balls. He will be happy that he has moved on.

Good effort from Broad, keeping Warner under pressure. Similar length ball, Warner drives it nicely towards Broad who gets low in his followthrough and gets a hand to it to parry it past the stumps at the other end.
Fullish delivery, driven crisply to mid off.

Looks for the slash to get to the three-figure mark but mistimes it completely. Back of a length outside off, a bit of room on offer. Warner looks to cut it but chops it besides the pitch on the off side. Nervy nineties tell you.

Anderson is having a chat with the umpire. S Ravi is gesturing to the veteran that he can't bowl right now as he was off the field since Lunch. The on-air commentators inform that he will be allowed to bowl only after another two minutes. So, Broad will continue his spell.
Full delivery attacking the stumps, patted to mid on.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Similar length ball, Usman drives it off the inner half of the bat to mid on.
Fuller in length outside off, eased off the front foot to covers.
This is poor from Khawaja. He needs to be patient. Shortish delivery outside off, Khawaja goes for a pull but gets beaten.
A play and a miss! Good ball from Woakes. On a length outside off, angling in. Khawaja looks to keep it out but the ball goes past his inside edge and through to the keeper.
Broad delivers it almost near the tramline, Warner watches it go through to the keeper. Broad smiles but the crowd Boos him!
Pitches it right up there, Warner drives it nicely but finds the man at short cover.
Too full and sprayed wide outside off, Warner lets it be.
Keeps it fuller outside off, wanting Warner to go after it but the southpaw remains calm. Leaves it alone.
Sprays it a bit wide outside off, David once again makes a leave.
Bowls a tempter does Broad. It's full and outside off, Warner doesn't play at it.
Fuller on off, driven straight to short cover. A successful over from Woakes!
A wide yorker, Khawaja jams it out.
From around the wicket comes Woakes and hurls it on a length on off, defended from within the crease.
Usman Khawaja strides out next to bat, replacing Bancroft.

OUT! Trapped in front! Cameron Bancroft is walking off, he knows he is a goner! England rejoice! Brilliant delivery from Woakes. Deserved it thoroughly. He was bowling shorter lines to Bancroft and then smartly changes the length to taste success. He comes steaming in and drops it near the good length area. The ball deviates off the pitch, stays a touch low and pings Cameron on the front pad as he looks to defend. They all appeal in jubilation and umpire Dharmasena has no qualms in raising his finger. Bancroft starts to walk back and England finally get a breakthrough. He didn't even bother discussing about the review with his partner. Hawk Eye shows it's pitched in line, impact is in line and would have clipped the top of the stumps. Umpire's call! End of a superb opening stand for Australia.
On a length and served in the channel outside off, Cameron defends it towards the off side solidly.
Length delivery outside off, defended towards cover.
Good running! Back of a length, but it's angling down leg. Warner gets across and tucks it towards backward square leg and calls for the second immediately. Gets it in the end.
Outside off, shouldered arms to.

FOUR! Superbbbb, says Bill Lawry on air. David Warner has totally nailed it down the ground! Was waiting for the ball to be a half volley and spanks as soon as he gets it there. Broad overcooks it and the southpaw is up for it. Leans into it and eases it off the meat past mid off for a boundary.
Ahead of a length on off, a solid front foot defense on offer from Warner.
There is some issue with the ball. Broad shows it to the umpire.
Angles it in around middle and leg, Bancroft shuffles a touch and clips it towards deep backward square leg for a single.
Back of a length delivery outside off, punched off the back foot towards the cover region.
Length delivery outside off, Warner initially decides to go after it but then resists and makes an easy leave.
Yorker, fired outside off, Warner jams it out towards the short cover fielder.
Woakes is getting some inward movement here but Warner blocks it down safely.
Fuller ball outside off, Warner backs away and drives it towards cover. The man at short cover gets a hand to it which slows the ball down. The batsmen take a couple.
Another effort ball but how long can Woakes bowl with the same venom! Another shortish one, Warner defends it off the back foot.
Woakes comes from around the wicket, bowls short and this one comes back in off the pitch. Warner looks to cut but gets an inside edge which evades the stumps.
Gets forward again does Cameron which is a good thing and eases it towards the man at mid on.
Good line! But keep it a bit more fuller, Broad! Bancroft doesn't fall and is happy to leave it alone.
Wasn't that off the middle? Seemed like! Fuller ball on off, Cameron leans ahead and drives it towards Malan at short cover.
Comes over the wicket to the right-hander, pitches it full on off, Cameron leans forward and bunts it back to Broad.
Fuller and angling in on the pads, wristed past the man at mid-wicket for an easy single.
Tight lines from Broad! Shortish and outside off, David defends it towards the off side.
Back of a length again, defended off the back foot back to the bowler.
Woakes goes wide of the crease, tries to angle the ball in but it's a bit too straight. Cameron walks across and works it through mid-wicket to get a brace. That should get Cameron going.
Chris goes short and bowls it outside off, the batsman remains patient as he allows it to go through to the keeper.
Pitches it right up there, maybe, because Bancroft edged one in the previous over. But this time from the middle of the bat, Cameron drives it towards mid off which is a tad straight for him.
Fuller in length and outside off, driven off the front foot but straight to the cover fielder.
Back of a length, bowled just around that off stump channel. CB shows a straight bat.
Woakes loses his run-up. He comes running in and just when he is about to deliver, a bird flies across the pitch which forces him to abort. Poor Chris has to go back...
Broad once again bowls it on a back of a length outside off, Warner could only defend it towards the off side. Good comeback from Broad after being hit for a boundary.
Taps this length delivery towards cover and says WAIT ON, straightaway to his partner.
Pitches it up on off, Warner goes hard at it, but mistimes it towards short cover.
On a length and served outside off, Warner hangs back in defense.
Back of a length delivery outside off, punched off the back foot towards cover.
